plan.title: Inspect repo sources
plan.detail: Read main.c and Makefile to understand the current firmware skeleton: clock config, I2C init, any existing BMP180 driver stubs, RTT setup, and build flags. No hardware interaction.

plan.title: Write BMP180 firmware
plan.detail: Edit main.c to implement: (1) HSI 8 MHz clock confirmed, (2) GPIO PB8/PB9 to AF4 open-drain for I2C1, (3) I2C1 init with TIMINGR for 100 kHz standard-mode at 8 MHz HSI, (4) BMP180 chip-ID read (reg 0xD0, expect 0x55), (5) read raw calibration coefficients AC1–AC6/B1/B2/MB/MC/MD from EEPROM (0xAA–0xBF), (6) trigger uncompensated temperature and pressure readings, (7) compute true temperature and pressure per BMP180 datasheet algorithm, (8) print chip-ID, temperature, and pressure over Segger RTT. Update Makefile if RTT sources are missing.

plan.title: Build firmware
plan.detail: Run `make clean && make` via build_firmware. Verify exit code 0 and that rtt-f303re.elf is produced.

plan.title: Flash firmware to board
plan.detail: Use flash_firmware (pyocd flash --target stm32f303retx rtt-f303re.elf). Requires human approval. Board is powered over USB/ST-LINK.

plan.title: Capture I2C traffic on logic analyzer
plan.detail: Run capture_during to arm the Kingst LA2016 (CH0=SDA, CH1=SCL) while the MCU executes the BMP180 sequence. Decode I2C frames: verify device ACK at 0x77, SCL frequency ~100 kHz, chip-ID byte 0x55 returned.

plan.title: Read RTT log
plan.detail: Call read_firmware_log to collect RTT output. Verify chip-ID printed as 0x55, temperature in a plausible range (15–40 °C), and pressure in a plausible range (90000–110000 Pa).

plan.title: Record all checks and write report
plan.detail: Call record_check for every registered check, citing artifact IDs from build log, LA capture, and RTT log. Then call write_report with a fully evidence-linked Markdown summary.

payload.riskSummary: Hardware mutations in this run: one flash operation (Step 4) that writes the compiled BMP180 firmware ELF to the STM32F303RE over the ST-LINK debug probe. This is the only destructive action; it overwrites flash but leaves SRAM/calibration data in the BMP180 EEPROM untouched. The flash step is approval-gated by the harness. A reset is implicit after flash (pyocd flash resets the target). No erase-only or mass-erase commands are issued. All other steps (source edits, build, LA capture, RTT read) are non-destructive. If the flash is rejected the run will end without any hardware mutation.
